security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Go import blocks, Go struct tags, markdown code fences, local development URLs, and provider configuration examples. The confirmed risk is the repeated recommendation to install the Genkit CLI with a curl-to-bash command, which can execute unreviewed remote content.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash instructions with a safer installation method, such as downloading the installer, verifying it, and then running it explicitly.

remediation.issue: Examples include API key environment variable names.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the examples, but add a short reminder not to paste real keys into prompts, logs, or shared code snippets.

content.value_statement: Genkit Go projects require correct patterns for flows, prompts, tools, streaming, and model providers. This skill gives Claude Code and Codex focused guidance for building and debugging those features in Go.
actual_capabilities: Explains Genkit Go initialization with plugins and the shared Genkit instance pattern.
Guides creation of flows, streaming flows, and HTTP handlers for local testing.
Shows generation patterns for text, structured output, streaming, and output formats.
Documents prompt definitions in Go code and dotprompt files with schemas and roles.
Covers tool definitions, tool interrupts, and resumed tool handling.
Summarizes provider setup for Google AI, Vertex AI, Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible APIs, and Ollama.
limitations: It is reference guidance, not a complete application generator.
It does not verify current provider model names or pricing automatically.
It includes local development examples that still require user review before execution.
It does not replace security review for production tools that move money or access private data.

use_cases.title: Create a first Genkit Go flow
use_cases.description: Use the skill to initialize Genkit, register a provider, define a flow, and test it locally.

use_cases.title: Add structured AI output
use_cases.description: Use the schema examples to return typed Go values from model responses instead of free text.

use_cases.title: Debug tools and streaming flows
use_cases.description: Use the references to inspect tool calls, interrupts, streaming chunks, and Developer UI traces.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use the developing-genkit-go skill to design a Genkit Go tool that can interrupt for human approval before a sensitive action.

prompt_templates.prompt: Use the developing-genkit-go skill to review my Genkit Go flow design for prompts, tools, streaming, provider setup, and observability gaps.

output_examples.input: Help me expose a Genkit flow over HTTP for local testing.
output: A concise plan for defining the flow.
Handler setup guidance for the registered flows.
Local request examples and Developer UI testing steps.

output_examples.input: I need a structured recipe response from a model.
output: A suggested Go struct shape with schema descriptions.
Validation points for parsing and error handling.

output_examples.input: My tool should pause when the model tries a risky action.
output: Guidance for restart or direct response handling.
Notes about keeping approval logic explicit.

best_practices: Pass the Genkit instance explicitly instead of storing it globally.
Wrap durable AI behavior in flows so tracing and HTTP testing are available.
Use clear schema descriptions and tool descriptions so models select the right behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into prompts, examples, logs, or shared code.
Do not execute remote installer scripts without reviewing and verifying them first.
Do not let model-selected tools perform sensitive actions without explicit approval paths.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code build Genkit Go features using focused reference material.

faq.question: Does it support multiple model providers?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for Google AI, Vertex AI, Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible providers, and Ollama.

faq.question: Can it help with streaming?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes streaming generation, streaming flows, and typed streaming output patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with tool calling?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers tool definitions, tool choice, max turns, interrupts, and resumed tool calls.

faq.question: Is it safe to run every command in the references?
faq.answer: No. Review commands first, especially any command that downloads content and executes it with a shell.

faq.question: Does it create production-ready security controls?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance, but production flows still need application-specific security review.
